title: Lesson 5. Capital letters and switching language
description: Shift, punctuation, Caps Lock and three languages

questions.prompt: What is the strongman key for capitals called?
questions.explain: Shift makes a letter big while you hold it.

questions.prompt: Caps Lock turns on capitals and they stay big until you turn it off.
questions.explain: It is "shouting" — press again to turn it off.

questions.prompt: Which combination usually switches the language?

questions.explain: Like in a notebook — with a capital.
A capital at the start and a period at the end.

questions.prompt: Match the word with the language
If you let go of Shift, the letters are small again.
questions.explain: Shift only works while you hold it.

learn.intro: Sentences start with a capital letter! Today we meet the strongman key and learn to type in different languages.

slides.text: **Shift** is the strongman key. Hold it — the letter becomes big. Let go — small again.
Both keys together are like a chord on a piano: Shift + letter.

check.prompt: How do you type a capital letter?
check.explain: Hold Shift and press the letter.

slides.text: Shift + the number 1 gives **!**. The keyboard also has a period, a comma and a question mark **?**.
**Caps Lock** turns on CAPITAL letters for good — like shouting. Press it again — off. If suddenly all letters are big — check Caps Lock!

check.prompt: If all letters suddenly became capitals, Caps Lock is probably on.
check.explain: Press Caps Lock again to turn it off.

slides.text: The computer knows many languages. At the bottom right you see **РУС** or **ENG** — the language we type in now.
Switch language: **Alt + Shift** or **Win + Space**. Type: Привет! → Hello! → Salom!

check.prompt: Where can you see which language you type in?
check.explain: It says РУС or ENG there.
